Documentation → Administration → Settings → Path Diagnostics settings

Path Diagnostics settings

Site settings for Path Diagnostics, the operator-started fault-isolation walk — whether it (and the Upgrade Advisory) is available, the walk-form defaults and the FortiAnalyzer border query — plus the read-only decision criteria a Path Diagnostics verdict is produced under.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics (URL /settings/#tab-scout)

What is it?#

Path Diagnostics walks a published service down ten layers and stops at the first one that fails, naming it. It is read-only and operator-started. Settings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics holds only where to look and how long to wait; what a verdict means is shown underneath as a read-only table, on purpose. Settings → AI → Scout → Architecture renders the ten rungs from the engine and is described in Path Diagnostics.

ℹ️Note

Renamed on 2026-10-14: this settings group was called Scout until then. Settings → AI → Scout → Providers is now the AI assistant's pane (see Scout settings). The anchor #tab-scout and the scout.<key> setting names are unchanged.

What does it do?#

  • Availability — switches Path Diagnostics on or off for the whole site. The Upgrade Advisory follows the same switch.
  • Walk defaults — values pre-filled into the Path Diagnostics walk form.
  • Border correlation (FortiAnalyzer) — defaults for the border rung's log query.
  • Decision criteria — read only — the live values of the rules a report is produced under (which phase is blamed, when a layer counts as broken, how the border is read, limits and precedence), each with the code symbol it is read from and Why it is not a knob.
  • Open Path Diagnostics links to the tool.

Requirements#

  • For the border rung: a FortiAnalyzer registered and receiving logs from the border devices.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

The pane is rendered only for administrators (users.manage), and saving (POST /settings/scout) requires the same key; anyone else gets 403 Forbidden, even with a direct request. There is no standalone page.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: saving these settings requires users.manage; before, any user with a change permission (for example the seeded operator profile) could save them, including switching the feature off, with a direct request.

How to use#

  1. Open Settings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics.
  2. Adjust the fields (each shows its key scout.<key> and a ?).
  3. Click Save Path Diagnostics settings. Flashes: "Path Diagnostics settings saved: N changed.", "Path Diagnostics settings unchanged.", and "Clamped to their allowed range: …" when a number was out of range.
  4. Read the Decision criteria — read only tables when interpreting a report.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Path Diagnostics is available Off closes the ladder and the Upgrade Advisory for everyone; the menu entry stays, disabled, saying why. Nothing is deleted. Default: on. No on
Default look-back window (minutes) Pre-filled into the walk form; how far back rung 7 asks the border for flows and rung 9 reads the attack log. Default: 30; range 1–1440. No 30
Front-door probe timeout (seconds) Per-request ceiling for the HTTP probe on rungs 3 and 8. Default: 8.0; range 1.0–30.0. No 8.0
Probe from the appliance by default Pre-ticks the SSH box on the walk form; each walk then opens an SSH session to the device. Default: off. No off
Default FortiAnalyzer ADOM ADOM the border rung searches. A wrong ADOM returns zero rows, reported as UNKNOWN. Default: root. No root
Default device id (devid) Narrows the border query to one logging device; blank = all. Default: empty. No —
Default VDOM Combined with the devid; blank = no VDOM restriction. Default: empty. No —
Rows per border query Upper bound on rows; truncation can change which verdict wins. Default: 200; range 1–1000. No 200
Border query timeout (seconds) Whole asynchronous search; expiry is reported as UNKNOWN. Default: 20.0; range 1.0–120.0. No 20.0

Numbers outside their range are clamped. The engine clamps the window and timeouts again at walk time.

Example#

🧪Example — Border devices log into a dedicated ADOM

Set Default FortiAnalyzer ADOM to border, leave devid and VDOM blank, raise Rows per border query to 500 because busy windows kept hitting the cap. Every new walk now queries that ADOM by default; operators can still change it per walk.

Result#

  • Values are stored in app_settings under scout.<key>; audit entry scout.settings with the changed keys.
  • The next walk form is pre-filled with the new defaults.

Troubleshooting#

"Clamped to their allowed range: …"#

Solution — the stored value is the clamped one; choose a value within the range shown above.

The border rung always reports UNKNOWN#

Possible causes — wrong ADOM, devid or VDOM (zero rows), a timeout, or a window too short.

Solution — correct the border defaults, raise the timeout or window, and walk again.

Path Diagnostics shows as disabled in the menu#

Possible causes — Path Diagnostics is available is off (it does not depend on the Scout providers above).

Solution — switch it on and save.

The Upgrade Advisory says "Turn on Path Diagnostics in Settings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics to see the Upgrade Advisory."#

Possible causes — the Upgrade Advisory (the firmware release-notes reviewer) uses the Path Diagnostics switch; Path Diagnostics is available is off.

Solution — switch it on here and save. The release-notes page offers the same switch to administrators.

Verification — the Upgrade Advisory card shows verdicts again on the Upgrade page and in Release Notes.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • Only the site settings are writable; a POST naming a criterion changes nothing.
  • Criteria values are read off the engine when the page renders, so the table cannot drift from the code.
  • If the Path Diagnostics module cannot be imported, the pane renders without fields instead of breaking the Settings page.
